segments.t: Outside the station, the senior detective explains to young Lieutenant Sudnik why he let Denis go: Denis is just a small-time courier who will lead them straight to the kingpin. Following Denis to the back courtyard of Claude Monet, they spot supplier Timur handing over crates and decide to infiltrate the restaurant.
Товарищ капитан, зачем вы его сейчас отпустили?
Включи наконец свою голову и подумай!
Этот молодой парень — просто мелкий курьер.
Через него мы выйдем на крупную рыбу!
Смотрите, он зашёл в этот дорогой ресторан.
Подождите, а это ещё кто во дворе?
А вот и серьёзные поставщики приехали сюда!
Мы напали на след большой группировки.
Но у нас пока нет прямых доказательств.
Значит, нам надо тихо внедриться внутрь.
Предлагаю назвать нашу секретную операцию «Ураган»!
Пошли в зал, там сейчас всё узнаем!
Let's walk through how the detectives launch their undercover operation.
Товарищ капитан, зачем вы его сейчас отпустили?
'Comrade Captain, why did you let him go just now?' Denis centers one memorable element in earnest: "tovarishch" means "comrade", and it carries the main weight of what Denis is saying.
Включи наконец свою голову и подумай!
'Turn on your head at last and think!' The inspector counters calmly hearing Denis, without trying to dress up how he really feels.
Этот молодой парень — просто мелкий курьер.
'This young guy is just a small-time courier.' The inspector answers promptly during the talk, grounding the moment in plain reality.
Через него мы выйдем на крупную рыбу!
'Through him we will get to the big fish!' The inspector colors one direct expression at once: "krupnuyu" means "large, prominent" (from "krupnyy"), giving the line its exact edge.
Смотрите, он зашёл в этот дорогой ресторан.
'Look, he went into this expensive restaurant.' Denis chimes in lightly around the inspector, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
Подождите, а это ещё кто во дворе?
'Wait, and who else is that in the courtyard?' Denis checks openly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
А вот и серьёзные поставщики приехали сюда!
'And here the serious suppliers have arrived here!' The inspector uses this vivid piece toward Denis: "postavshchiki" means "supplier, purveyor" (from "postavshchik"), giving the line its exact edge.
Мы напали на след большой группировки.
'We have hit the trail of a major syndicate.' The inspector steps in frankly without a pause, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
Но у нас пока нет прямых доказательств.
'But we do not have direct evidence yet.' Denis speaks openly with the inspector, before the inspector can change the subject.
Значит, нам надо тихо внедриться внутрь.
'That means we need to quietly infiltrate inside.' The inspector leans on this clear piece in earnest: "vnedritsya" means "to inside", and it carries the main weight of what the inspector is saying.
Предлагаю назвать нашу секретную операцию «Ураган»!
'I propose naming our secret operation Hurricane!' Denis answers candidly in their talk, before the inspector can change the subject.
Пошли в зал, там сейчас всё узнаем!
'Let's go into the dining room, we will find out everything there now!' The inspector reacts evenly around Denis, steering the talk right where he wants it.

Determined to catch the culinary syndicate red-handed, the two detectives head into the dining room posing as guests. Next, Katya begins her molecular show-kitchen. Until next time!
